chapter_title: Concerning the Five Storehouses that have poured f

16.content: who belong to the world of

spiritual_reading:
From the first arising of a state of denial of good and truth, a sufficient number of interior reservoirs of evil and falsity were opened within that domain. From those interiors a sufficient series of fundamental perversions flowed forth. From those perversions were organized fixed systems of perverted perception; and from those systems were produced complete kinds of disordered affections and thoughts in every degree of life, each joined in a counterfeit union of will and understanding. In each such degree there rules a sufficient set of dominant loves, together with their persuasive spirits, their embodied forms of habit and compulsion, and their delights of appropriation; and in each degree these are unlike the others, because each degree has its own quality of evil and falsity.

The ruling love that presides over the obscuring persuasion that rises from the lowest denial is the source from which the whole complex of malice takes its head. Through this love the first impulse to spiritual conflict was released: contention against truth, assaults upon good, mutual hatred, peril to what is living, and the destruction of what could be reformed. This love first set in motion the lust of domination and opposition, together with its organized degrees and its operative forces. Afterward it also turned itself against the influx of wisdom, and set itself in direct opposition to the higher government of good and truth.

In that chief ruling evil there is a full set of outward appearances that display the quality of the whole. In its highest level it is a proud and cruel confidence in its own power; in its actions it is the delight of doing harm and of subjugating; in what upholds and bears its rule it is a lofty, far-seeing craft; in its inmost craving it is the devouring appetite to possess and consume what is another’s; and in its ultimate extension it is a cold, sensuous persuasion that drags everything down to mere outward knowing. These are the full signs of the principal degrees within that kingdom of denial.

There are also within it a sufficient set of ruling qualities. One is the absence of wisdom that it calls its own light. Another is the corruption of every affection for good. Another is the deforming of all truth into what serves self. Another is the interior sting and bitterness that it experiences as its life. The last is the burning zeal of self-love, which inflames as if it were strength, and acts with a harsh, unyielding fervor.

There are further qualities in it that resist all amendment. One is that its formed character is stiff and unbending, because it is shaped from the intention of spiritual death, and thus from a will set against heaven. That intention, being the very origin of its formation, makes its confirmed state hard to break by any ordinary means of correction; for it has been made firm in itself by repeated acts, and therefore does not easily yield or submit.

Also, the chief ruling evil has a shrewd perception of the utterances and reasonings that arise within its subordinate degrees. It catches the sound and manner of their persuasions, and understands what is being exchanged among them in their several modes of falsity. It perceives the schemes by which they would protect themselves, and the devices by which they would shift blame or evade restraint; it even notices the silent signs by which they agree together. Yet those subordinate forces do not similarly grasp the deeper purposes of the ruling evil, nor the full reach of its craft. Although much is laid open to that chief love, it does not penetrate to the inner intentions of others as they are in themselves; it does not truly know their ruling ends, nor can it comprehend the whole course of their designs from first to last. It apprehends only what is present and immediate, what lies in its current awareness.

Moreover, it can alternately expand itself into active power and contract itself into a compact, oppressive presence. When it is stirred to act, it sends its influences outward into many operations. When it turns back into itself, it draws its operations inward and becomes a concentrated weight among its allies, pressing downward into the lowest loves. It terrifies by the violence of its persuasive outcry; it shakes its subordinate forces by the sheer force of its asserted certainty. When it speaks, it sounds like overwhelming persuasion that drowns discernment; and when it summons its own, weaker impulses and subordinate falsities are driven into tremor and collapse, as thoughts without support fall when a stronger persuasion sweeps over them. Yet for all this, it has no true foresight: it does not perceive what is remote in consequence, nor what lies outside its immediate sphere. It recognizes and attends only to what is directly before it.

These are the signs and evil impressions found in the chief love of infernal persuasion, the head of all those who are in the delights of doing harm, brought forth by a domain of denial and nourished by cruelty, wickedness, and wrath, surpassing the other ruling evils that preside in its several degrees.

In the degree where falsity is most glittering and most convincing in externals, the embodied form of that ruling evil is a show of preciousness without genuine worth, and the whole company of its subordinate forces appears in the same kind of splendor. The delight by which it appropriates what it produces is a harsh and biting relish, because it delights in desolating and in making what is living barren.

In contrast, in the degree where self-love burns openly as dominant zeal, the ruling evil is marked by proud confidence as chief among brutish affections. Its embodied form is the hardness of outward good turned to use for self; and the forms of all its subordinate rulers are similar. The delight by which it appropriates is a pervasive sourness, because even what seems lively in it is inwardly hostile to innocence.

Again, in the degree where persuasion is volatile and domineering in thought, the ruling evil is marked by lofty craft in reasoning. Its embodied form is rigid severity in truthless confidence; and the forms of all who belong to that persuasion are of the same kind. The delight by which it appropriates is a sharpness that cuts, because it delights in disputation and in wounding truth.

In the degree where truth is falsified and made to serve sensuous pleasure, the ruling evil is marked by a cold, outward intelligence. Its embodied form is a pale appearance of truth without life; and the forms of its subordinate rulers are similar. The delight by which it appropriates is a sweetness that seems gentle, because falsity can mimic truth and thus insinuate itself pleasantly into the natural mind.

Finally, in the degree of active denial itself, the ruling evil is the devouring craving that destroys all spiritual life. Its embodied form is the heaviness and baseness of what is merely ultimate and earthly, compounded of gross falsity with its dull confirmations; and the forms of all who belong to that denial are of the same kind. The delight by which it appropriates is bitterness, because it hates good and therefore feels good as torment.

Also, the persuasive spirit that reigns in these states continues to speak wherever falsity claims revelation apart from heaven: in those who utter predictions from self-intelligence, in every kind of deceptive sign-making, in states where another’s falsity takes possession of the mind, and in all varieties of pretended inspiration that draw their voice not from the Divine but from the lower loves.

fills.notes: The passage immediately defines this king as the head-source of malice and the initiator of war. In the oldest cosmological register this is stated as a simple identification: the Smoke-king is the ruling principle rising from the depth.

The triad here describes (1) bodily hardness formed by Matter, (2) an interior quality of heart, and (3) (in ¶8) linguistic cunning. The second item must mark his interior as merciless in the active sense; pairing “evil and cruel-hearted” preserves the impersonal, descriptive substrate style and matches the subsequent attribution to Matter as ‘thought of death’.

The sentence requires a verb meaning that no implement can do this to him ‘and cut him’. In the substrate logic this property signifies unyielding confirmed state; ‘break’ is the natural correspondent that pairs with ‘cut’.
The closing restatement intensifies the fashioning by Matter: ‘has formed him exceedingly strong and hard’ fits the correspondential emphasis on confirmed rigidity.
Thunder-like speech is then compared to something ‘of the rocks’; the natural image required is the crashing or bursting sound that corresponds to overwhelming persuasion that drowns discernment.
Completes the simile: thunder in clouds resembles the crash of rocks when split. This keeps the impersonal, physical correspondence imagery typical of the oldest layer.
The sequence is: he cries out and does something and calls over his powers. The missing verb should be an intensified vocal action parallel to crying: ‘roars’.
Completes ‘calls ... over his powers’ in the sense of a summoning shout; fits the terrification motif.
The bird-comparison describes weaker powers collapsing when swept by a stronger outcry; ‘driven by the bird …’ preserves the correspondence of being carried and cast down by a stronger force.
A predatory bird best fits the image of lesser birds falling when driven by a stronger one; ‘hawk’ keeps the substrate’s concrete natural imagery without later moralizing labels.

fills.fill: who is the foremost of them,
fills.notes: This clause must resume the identification: the king is chief among demons and fiends; the lacuna bridges to ‘the one to whom… has given birth’. Restoring a superlative headship statement matches the correspondential summary in the spiritual translation.

The closing birth-formula in the oldest layer typically adds a nurturing image after ‘begotten in cruelty, wickedness, wrath’. ‘Reared’ keeps the structural cosmogonic tone; ‘poison’ corresponds to the domain’s corrupting nurture without importing later pastoral language.

assessment: Most gaps are locally constrained by the chapter’s fixed descriptive schema: kings, bodies (metals), tastes, and the king’s three further properties (hardness, cruel heart, linguistic cunning). The hardest restorations are in ¶9 (the thunder-rock simile and the bird comparison) and ¶10’s closing nurture clause, where the correspondential direction is clear (overwhelming outcry; birth and corrupt nurture) but several natural images could fit, so those readings remain tentative.
